text: A reputed private commercial bank known for its wide customer base, has recently been facing a growing number of customer complaints related to service quality. Customers frequently report long waiting times at cash counters, loan desks account opening, and grievance handling sections, leading to frustration and overcrowding. In addition, there are repeated transaction errors, including incorrect entries, duplicate charges, and delays in resolving failed transfers, which reduce customer trust. Another major concern is poor coordination between departments where lack of communication between front office, operations, credit, and IT teams leads to inefficiencies and confusion. Although the bank maintains sound financial stability and compliance standards, these operational issues have significantly affected the overall customer experience and satisfaction. In an effort to address these challenges, management introduced a new banking software system, expecting it to streamline operations and reduce errors. However the problems persist due to inadequate staff training, inconsistent use of the system and absence of standardized procedures. Departments continue to function in isolations and there is no structured approach to monitor or improve quality. Customer feedback is collected but not systematically analysed, and there are no clear performance metrics or accountability mechanisms. As a result, the bank is experiencing declining customer trust and increased competitive pressure. • Apply Crosby’s philosophy to identify the quality issues in this bank. •   Explain the meaning of zero defects in banking services and propose a practical improvement plan.

text: Shivam Infra Build Pvt. Ltd., a reputed construction company headquartered in Surat has been experiencing increasing pressure to improve productivity, ensure worker safety, reduce project delays, and remain competitive in a technology- driven construction environment. To address these challenges, the company’s CEO, Mr. Arvind Mehta, has proposed the introduction of a fleet of automated equipments including smart excavators, automated material-handling machines digital surveying tools, and sensor-based safety systems. The management expects these technologies to improve efficiency, reduce rework, and support better project execution. However, the initiative has encountered strong resistance from employees. Workers, supervisors, and construction engineers are skeptical about the new systems and fear that automation may reduce the value of their experience create job insecurity, and increase dependence on unfamiliar technology. The reluctance of employees has created uncertainty in the organization, and the implementation process has slowed down. Mr. Arvind Mehta understands that successful adoption of automation depends not only on technical investment but also on employee acceptance, motivation, and commitment to change. He believes that the workforce must be convinced that automation is a tool for improving performance, not a threat to employment. At the same time, he wants to build a culture in which employees recognize the need for continuous improvement innovation, and adaptation in order to sustain business growth and competitiveness. • What leadership approach should Mr. Arvind Mehta use to reduce employee resistance to automation and encourage a culture of continuous improvement in Shivam Infra Build Pvt. Ltd.?
